problems.title: Additive calibration conflicts with the defining transmission integral
problems.source_location: Current arXiv v2 Section 6, PDF p.7, Eq.(7); Appendix B.1–B.2, PDF pp.21–22
claim: Section 6, Eq.(7), uses \(T_r=T_p-C_p(0)+C_r(0)\) to calibrate reused-ray transmittance. Appendix B defines density from the clipped logarithmic derivative of the logistic CDF \(C\).
analysis: On a monotone entering ray the integral gives \(T(u)=C(u)/C(0)\). Use the true planar SDF \(f=(x+z)/\sqrt2\) and unit logistic scale. Origins \((0,0,\sqrt2\log3)\) and \((-\sqrt2\log2,0,\sqrt2\log3)\) lie in the same aperture plane and have CDFs \(3/4\), \(3/5\); choose their common endpoint at CDF \(1/2\). Then \(T_p=2/3\), but additive calibration gives \(31/60\), while the receiver ray requires \(5/6\). All values are finite and positive, and both straight rays are monotone for this planar SDF.
result: The central calibration formula is not derived from the stated density, even before nonmonotone path complications. No reconstruction benchmark is remeasured.
assumptions: The SDF is exact, unit-gradient and planar; both rays enter monotonically and the logistic scale is one.
repair: For monotone entering rays, the correct origin adjustment is \(T_r=T_pC_p(0)/C_r(0)\). General paths instead depend on accumulated downward variation of \(\log C\), so this endpoint ratio is not a universal ray-reuse repair.
problems.impact_rationale: The core lensless rendering formula has a large direct error on an admissible exact geometry.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The printed magnitude derivative omits the complex resultant
problems.source_location: Current arXiv v2 Appendix A.5, PDF p.19, Eq.(13); Algorithm 1, PDF p.20
claim: Appendix A.4 differentiates \(P_j=|z_j|\) but omits the resultant needed in its magnitude derivative.
analysis: For one positive real input with coefficient \(1\) and signal \(2\), \(P=2\), true derivative is \(1\), while the printed rule gives \(1/P=1/2\). This real subcase avoids complex-gradient convention ambiguity. The later `rf_rendering.py` instead computes real/imaginary outputs followed by `torch.hypot`, which retains the needed chain rule.
result: The printed formula is wrong; a current released gradient defect and historical benchmark effect are not established.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: For \(z\ne0\), use \(d|z|=\operatorname{Re}(\bar z\,dz)/|z|\), with a declared convention for the final real-loss complex gradient and the zero boundary.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a printed local derivative error with an important correct implementation countercontrol.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
